title: Playing the same hits nightly and the need to arrange for yourself
summary: Even good hits wore thin night after night; to advance you had to write your own arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well Herman, so far as playing the same thing every night, that's part of what you're talking about. When you're with a successful band, or when you get a band that's got a real hot hit, you've got to play it all the time. what happens?

Well that's bad enough, but it's as you say, a hit, and it's got to be good to be a hit, so that you don't mind, but I mean you sit there night after night, and you play those things, and you wonder why they guy bought them, you know, and you -- so -- I don't know. You're not happy. You're not -- and in those days, that's what counted. You were trying to establish the mood. You wanted to go forward. You was hoping someday, well, if I get with this guy, and he'll enable me to get with another guy bigger and better, maybe one day I'll hit tops. I mean that's what's always in back of your mind. That's what you're hoping for.
And to do that you had to be playing something. So -- and --

Something good, yeah, because I mean you couldn't use your own ideas all the time, and I mean to advance. You'd be lucky maybe to get in a nice hot chorus, hot lick, as they call it, or something good, and somebody would say anh, pretty good. But I mean to get it on record, on paper, I mean you had to be responsible, you had to be an arranger yourself.
